title: TBO implementation of WeakService using WinReg & BackupPrivs
description:
Migrated from Titanis-b5q.

Enumerate services remotely via winreg, check DACL for interesting entries. Similar to WeakService sample
design:
Base logic on C:\Data\Repos\Titanis\samples\msrpc\WeakServices\Program.cs

Instead of connecting to SCM over RPC, iterate through HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services using TBO-Reg or backupintent registry functions in TBO.  

Collect data on each service from it's key including Key Name, ImagePath, ObjectName, Start, Type, ErrorControl, DisplayName, and the binary security descriptor encoded as a reg binary in the child Security\Security value.  This should be a cmdlet along the lines of Get-TBORegServices. The security descriptor should be cast to a portable titanis security descriptor by default for cross-platform support, but a cmdlet switch -AsWindows should allow casting it as a RawSecurityDescriptor.

The object that Get-TBORegServices returns can then be parsed with similar logic as the WeakServices example in a cmdlet named Find-TBORegWeakServices. An example use would be piping Get-TBORegServices to Find-TBORegWeakServices

title: retrieve plaintext service account creds
description:
Migrated from Titanis-1xc.

Implement this gist as a function based on TBOReg cmdlets: https://gist.github.com/jborean93/58bba8236fac313e3d4b3970b8213cb6
design:
The gist provided would not provide all of the information needed to derive the hashes from the _SC_service\Security\.Default) value's byte array.  The Syskey needs to be recreated from the Class name of several HKLM\Ssytem\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA child keys.

The Syskey is constructed from the class name of the following keys:
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\JD
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Skew1
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\GBG
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Data

The python code at https://github.com/AlessandroZ/LaZagne/blob/858ff6f95f5176ae3c3c50a3ffc86723bf500a99/Windows/lazagne/softwares/windows/creddump7/win32/lsasecrets.py#L169 is a better approximation of how to get the secrets for a service account from the registry.

I've changed this to an epic as there should be child tasks created for:
- Construct the Syskey from the above LSA keys along with any other data required to decrypt other registry secrets such as the bootkey and LsaKey 
- [Titanis.Tbo.Smb2.PowerShell.TBOSD] helpers to use the info above to:
  - Decrypt a service account credential 
  - Decrypt the machine account credential
  - Decrypt an autologon credential
  - Decrypt SAM credentials
  - Decrypt LSA secrets
notes:
The code in these repositories may also be helpful:
https://github.com/G0ldenGunSec/SharpSecDump/blob/master/SharpSecDump/Program.cs

https://github.com/brandonprry/gray_hat_csharp_code/tree/master/ch14_reading_offline_hives

And the Get-PostHashdumpScript function at https://github.com/darkoperator/Posh-SecMod/blob/master/PostExploitation/PostExploitation.psm1

title: Review whether PSBuildModule is a good choice
description:
Migrated from Titanis-p2c.

Uses British spelling of Artefacts instead of artifacts and other oddieties.  Talk to Jake about this

comments.author: JimSykora
comments.text:
Here’s a focused, repo‑specific way to evaluate PSBuildModule before you decide to ditch it.

What PSBuildModule gives you (when it works)

Repeatable packaging: deterministic layout, packed/unpacked artefacts, manifest generation.
Manifest/meta hygiene: consistent ModuleVersion, Tags, ProjectUri, etc. from METADATA.md.
Binary conflict handling: ResolveBinaryConflicts* is handy when you have mixed deps.
Gallery‑ready outputs: zip + staged folder in one run.
What it costs you (what you’ve already hit)

Fragility: manifest parsing issues, missing RootModule, and PowerShellVersion formatting errors.
Opaque failures: a failing build can be hard to diagnose vs a simple dotnet build + copy.
Tooling overhead: dependency on PSPublishModule + build config files.
Side effects: past accidental edits to doc/UserGuide/tools and module layout inconsistencies.
Decision framework (what matters most for TBO)

Local dev loop speed
If dotnet build + copy is faster and more reliable for day‑to‑day testing, that’s a big win.
Release process reliability
If PSBuildModule still breaks intermittently or requires manual fixes, it’s a net negative.
Module correctness
If PSBuildModule sometimes generates incorrect manifests (RootModule/PowerShellVersion), it’s risky.
Reproducibility
If your “manual” path yields consistent, clean outputs and you can document it, you may not need it.
A pragmatic path forward

Keep PSBuildModule only for release packaging, not dev builds.
Use Build-Module.ps1 only when producing a release artefact; use dotnet build + copy for testing.
Add a documented “manual build” path as the default (already mostly in Docs/Usage.md).
Gate PSBuildModule usage behind a -UsePsBuildModule switch or separate script.
If PSBuildModule stays: lock the versions and add a sanity check script that validates the produced .psd1 (RootModule, PowerShellVersion, FormatsToProcess, etc.) before publish.
Quick litmus test
If you can’t get 3 consecutive PSBuildModule builds to produce a valid module folder without edits, it’s not a net positive right now.

If you want, I can draft a short comparison matrix and a “go/no‑go” checklist you can keep in the repo.

Some of the fragility costs were due to the project being nested inside the complex titanis project.  The accidental edits to markdown was due to building titanis, not psbuildmodule.  I don't like that it uses the british spelling of Artefacts.

I do like the idea of having a script that handles repeatable packaging, conflict handling, and gallery-ready outputs.

Got it — that changes the calculus.

If the earlier fragility was mostly from the nested Titanis build, then PSBuildModule might be worth keeping as a release‑only packaging step, while day‑to‑day testing stays on dotnet build + copy. That gives you the repeatable packaging/conflict handling you want without slowing the dev loop.

About the “Artefacts” spelling
That’s just PSPublishModule’s default naming; we can override the output paths in the build script so the repo uses Artifacts/ and never touches Artefacts/. If the tool insists on internal Artefacts/, we can:

redirect PSBuildModule output to Artifacts/ via the New-ConfigurationArtefact -Path ... values, or
create a thin compatibility folder (junction) so you still get a clean Artifacts/ tree.
Suggested middle ground

Keep PSBuildModule for release packaging only.
Add a Package-Module.ps1 wrapper (or -UsePsBuildModule switch) that:
validates metadata/manifest,
runs Build-Module,
verifies output module folder imports cleanly,
writes outputs to Artifacts/ (US spelling).
Keep Build-Module.ps1 optional and document both paths in Docs.
If you’re aligned, I can:

update the build script to use Artifacts/ and document it,
add a packaging smoke‑check (Import‑Module + Get‑Command check),
make PSBuildModule explicitly “release‑only” in Docs.
Want me to implement those changes now, or just draft a short decision checklist in Docs?

Middle ground sounds good. Proceed.  But we do need to track (beads issue likely) that PSBuildModule does need to be validated end-to-end once all this is in place.
